title: Spine-containing unions of consecutive interval faces are Segal-local equivalences
statement:
Use the small simplicial spaces, representables $F(m)$, mapping simplicial sets $\operatorname{Map}$ and Reedy model structure of [lem-coef-simplicial-space-reedy-cartesian]. For $m\geq1$, let $G(m)\subseteq F(m)$ be the union of all consecutive edges, with $G(1)=F(1)$. For integers $0\leq a<b\leq m$, let $F([a,b])\subseteq F(m)$ be the image of $F(b-a)$ under the injection $j\mapsto a+j$ for $0\leq j\leq b-a$. Let $\mathcal I$ be a finite collection of such intervals and put $H=\bigcup_{[a,b]\in\mathcal I}F([a,b])$. Assume $G(m)\subseteq H$. Let $V$ be a small Reedy fibrant simplicial space such that, for every $r\geq2$, its consecutive-edge comparison $V_r\to V_1\times_{V_0}\cdots\times_{V_0}V_1$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Then restriction induces a weak homotopy equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}(F(m),V)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}(H,V).$$
